findings.problem: The proof spends five lines re-deriving, by unfolding MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_apply and applying simp, the value of finSuccEquiv at a variable. That value is already covered by the named Mathlib lemma MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_X_zero. The same pattern recurs in planeCurveToBivariate_X_one (lines 70-76), where the inline argument unfolds finSuccEquiv_apply, rewrites Fin.succ with `show (1 : Fin 2) = Fin.succ (0 : Fin 1)`, and closes with rfl. That is a hand-rolled substitute for MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_X_succ. In both proofs the local lemma hinner is used only once, in `rw [hinner]`.
findings.proposed_change:
In planeCurveToBivariate_X_zero, delete hinner and use the Mathlib lemma directly after the existing `change`, i.e. keep
  rw [planeCurveToBivariate]
  change Polynomial.map (MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv K (Fin 1)).toRingHom
    (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv K 1 (MvPolynomial.X 0)) = Polynomial.X
then replace `rw [hinner]` with `rw [MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_X_zero]`, keeping the closing `simp`. Apply the same change to planeCurveToBivariate_X_one: replace the inline hinner proof with a step that rewrites the index to Fin.succ 0 and then applies MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_X_succ. Both replacements are sketches and were not compiled.
findings.benefit: The reader sees a named statement of the mathematical fact that finSuccEquiv sends the variable to the polynomial variable, instead of a definitional unfolding whose correctness depends on the internals of finSuccEquiv_apply. The statements of the two `planeCurveToBivariate_X_*` simp lemmas stay visible: the outer variable becomes Polynomial.X and the inner variable becomes Polynomial.C Polynomial.X.

The other bullets (`exact hdegreeFirst`, `exact hdegreeSecond`, `exact hsize`, `exact hdegreeAlternativeExcluded`) do no work: they pass through hypotheses that already have exactly the needed type. The same pass-through pattern appears at lines 546-554 of planeCurve_auxiliaryFamily_linearIndependent_of_absoluteIrreducible_coordinateDegrees. These bullet lists make the reader check, one item at a time, whether some hidden manipulation occurs, when in fact none does.
